newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dow makes 2 billion rand S.Africa bid.
newsitem.headline: Dow makes 2 billion rand S.Africa bid.

text.p: United States chemical giant Dow Chemical Co on Monday said it had made a 2.074 billion rand ($446 million) bid for South African chemicals firm Sentrachem Ltd.
Dow has an agreement from investment firm Sankorp Ltd, which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem, to accept and recommend the 10.50 rand a share offer.
"We have agreed to accept Dow's offer and make the same positive recommendation to the minority shareholders of Sentrachem," said Sankorp executive director and Sentrachem chairman Attie du Plessis.

Sentrachem, with annual sales of 5.5 billion rand, has its main businesses in speciality chemicals and agricultural chemicals. It also operates in polypropylene, polyethylene, latex and rubber products.
Dow first entered the South African market in 1959 but pulled out during the 1980s as firms faced pressure to disinvest from the former white-ruled state.

However, the firm returned to South Africa after an eight year absence in 1995, a year after the country's first fully democratic elections, to operate a polyurethane plant near Durban on the Indian Ocean coast.

"This acquisition reinforces our strategic direction to enhance Dow's performance-chemicals portfolio with the addition of Sentrachem's strong speciality and agricultural chemicals businesses, among others," said William Stavropoulos, Dow chief executive and president.
Dow is the world's fifth largest chemicals company with annual sales of more than $20 billion, about 40,000 employees and customers in 157 countries.

Sentrachem has been going through a troubled period recently. It embarked on a huge restructuring programme in June after it posted a first half pre-tax loss of 257 million rand following one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at its Sanachem unit.
However, if the Dow purchase goes ahead -- as seems likely -- certain key elements of the restructuring are likely to come under review.

Sentrachem managing director John Job said some possible disposals and a study into listing a speciality chemicals firm based around its Hampshire Chemicals unit in London or New York, would now be looked at again.

But Job added that many of the cost-cutting elements of the restructuring would still go ahead. They included moves such as a merger of its NCP and Karbochem units and plans to cut costs by 300-350 million rand at its Sanachem unit.

The bid news first broke when the Johannesburg Stock Exchange suspended Sentrachem's listing pending an announcement. But the market welcomed the news and the offer's healthy premium on the firm's last closing share price of 7.92 rand.
"It is about time Sentrachem came out with some good news," said Peer Ieul, managing director at UAL Securities.
